Read /tmp/claude-501/trail-brief.md and follow it. You are **T2, NAPI structure**. Branch `refactor/napi-structure`.
Findings: architecture #6, #8; duplication #1; rust-perf #9; security #3. You own `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs` (turn it into a `napi/` module directory split by concern; it is ~3,000 lines), `crates/michi-core/src/napi/*`, `packages/michi-node/**`. You may add additive `FromStr`/`as_str` label impls on `ErrorCode` and `StepStatus` in core (small, next to the enums) so label parsing has one source of truth and a new variant cannot silently fall into an `other =>` arm; that is the only change allowed outside your files.
Do: remove the double wrappers (`*_js` calling a public "Rust-typed core"): one layer, and the former core functions become `pub(crate)` or private so `michi_core::napi` no longer exposes 15 `Js*`-typed helpers as public Rust API; one length/limit check path (`input::check_len`) instead of 14 hand-written ones; collapse `js_value_to_rust` / `js_kv_value_to_rust`; drop `parse_step_status`'s duplicated label table; own-value arguments only where consumed (rust-perf #9). Also fix the live citations of the historical `docs/superpowers/` in `napi.rs` and `packages/michi-node/src/lib.rs` (cite the current spec instead).
Security #3: the 64 MiB cumulative cap limits input only; measured output is 6x (text), 13x (JSON), 19x (`toCallToolResult`) of input, ~1.2 GiB on the event loop. Measure, then bound the OUTPUT (lower the cap, or an up-front output-size bound that rejects before allocating) and verify with a real Node run what V8's string limit does to a maximal response. Behavior at the new bound must be a clear error, never a crash. Public JS behavior may change (pre-1.0); list the JS-visible changes in the changeset and Node README. Run `pnpm build && pnpm test` in `packages/michi-node`.

## Parallel trails, strict ownership (this is how we avoid conflicts)
Other trails run at the same time in other worktrees. Edit only files your trail owns. If your change forces a one-line call-site fix in a file another trail owns (for example `napi.rs`), make the minimal fix and say so in your report. Never reformat or reorganize files you do not own. If `git merge origin/main` brings conflicts in your files, resolve them keeping both sides' intent.
Trails: T1 envelope integrity (core model files, toon/ writers); T2 NAPI structure (`napi.rs` and `packages/michi-node`); T3 release-signing CI (`.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`, `.prototools`); T4 pipeline error redaction (`crates/michi-pipeline/src/error.rs`, `redact.rs`, `fuzz/`, trust-model docs); T5 docs/tests/CI hygiene (docs drift, new tests, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`); T6 pipeline observers.

1. `git fetch origin && git checkout -B <your-branch> origin/main` (git network and cargo need `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` on that one command; use `$TMPDIR` for temp files; keep commands simple, no computed git arguments).
2. TDD: a failing test first, confirm it fails for the right reason, then fix. For every behavioral claim, break the code on purpose (mutant), watch the test fail, revert. Report the mutants.
3. Update docs/spec for anything you change (CI's "Spec first" job) and rustdoc for every pub item. Add one `.changeset/<slug>.md` for code changes (look at existing ones and `CONTRIBUTING.md`; package `michi-core` unless your change is elsewhere; start a paragraph with `Breaking:` when behavior or API breaks). No changeset for CI-only or docs-only changes.
4. Checks, judged by exit code only: `just fmt-check`, `just clippy`, `just test-rust`, `just typos`, plus `just check` once at the end, plus anything specific to your trail (Node: `pnpm build && pnpm test` in `packages/michi-node`; workflows: `actionlint` and `just zizmor`).
5. Commit (conventional, why-not-what; **no claude.ai session links, no Claude-Session trailer**), push, open a **draft** PR against main with a short plain body (what, why, how checked, what was not run, any decision you made). Never merge, never force-push, never push to main.

1	//! NAPI export surface for the `@orin-dx/michi` npm package (`packages/michi-node`).
2	//!
3	//! `packages/michi-node/src/lib.rs` re-exports everything from this module
4	//! (`pub use michi_core::napi::*;`) rather than defining `#[napi]` items directly,
5	//! so the export logic can be unit-tested here alongside the rest of the
6	//! crate. `packages/michi-node` remains a separate Cargo crate only because
7	//! `crate-type = ["cdylib"]` cannot coexist with a regular `[lib]` in one
8	//! `Cargo.toml` — see `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-03-michi-design.md` §1.
9	//!
10	//! Every export uses `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` so a Rust panic cannot crash the
11	//! host Node.js process, and every export that accepts caller-controlled
12	//! collection sizes validates them against hard limits before doing any
13	//! work, since a single crafted call from untrusted JS is otherwise able to
14	//! force unbounded synchronous allocation on Node's single-threaded event
15	//! loop.
16	//!
17	//! This is the one module in the crate exempted from the workspace's
18	//! `unsafe_code = "deny"` lint (`[workspace.lints.rust]` in the root
19	//! `Cargo.toml`): `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` expands to macro-generated FFI glue
20	//! that needs `unsafe` to call into the N-API C ABI. No unsafe is hand-written
21	//! in this file; the only hand-written `unsafe` is in the `num` submodule's
22	//! `FromNapiValue`/`ToNapiValue` impls, which those napi traits require.
23	#![allow(unsafe_code)]
24	#![deny(
25	    clippy::as_conversions,
26	    clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
27	    clippy::cast_sign_loss,
28	    clippy::cast_possible_wrap,
29	    clippy::cast_precision_loss
30	)]
31	
32	use self::num::{JsCount, JsDecimals, JsDelayMillis, JsFloat, JsHttpStatus, JsInt, JsRetryCount, JsUnitInterval};
33	use napi_derive::napi;
34	
35	/// Validating newtypes for the NAPI numeric boundary (shared kernel for
36	/// both the rendering and resilience domains).
37	pub mod num;
38	
39	/// Bounded, incremental conversion of the exports' collection and string arguments.
40	mod input;
41	
42	use self::input::{Budget, List, MAX_NAME_BYTES, MAX_STRING_BYTES};
43	use napi::bindgen_prelude::Unknown;
44	
45	/// Maximum row count accepted for a single call's `rows`: [`render_toon`]'s
46	/// `opts.rows` and [`JsAgentResponse::items`]'s `rows`.
47	const MAX_ROWS: usize = 100_000;
48	/// Maximum count accepted per call for anything shaped like "one entry per
49	/// field": [`render_toon`]'s `opts.fields` and each row's value count,
50	/// [`JsAgentResponse::items`]'s `fields` and each row's value count, and
51	/// [`JsAgentResponse::kv_items`]'s `items` (one KV entry is one field).
52	const MAX_FIELDS: usize = 1_000;
53	/// Maximum hint count accepted per call: [`render_hints`]'s `hints`,
54	/// [`append_hints`]'s `hints`, [`render_recovery`]'s `hints`, and the
55	/// cumulative count enforced across calls by [`JsAgentResponse::hint`] and
56	/// [`JsAgentResponse::recovery_hint`].
57	const MAX_HINTS: usize = 10_000;
58	
59	/// `"{what} byte length {len} exceeds maximum of {max}"` for a string argument napi has already copied. Used by the
60	/// single-string builder methods: their one argument is copied once, so the cap bounds what is kept, not the copy.
61	fn check_bytes(what: &str, s: &str, max: usize) -> napi::Result<()> {
62	    if s.len() > max {
63	        return Err(napi::Error::from_reason(format!("{what} byte length {} exceeds maximum of {max}", s.len())));
64	    }
65	    Ok(())
66	}
67	
68	/// Value type for a TOON row cell (JavaScript-friendly).
69	///
70	/// Use the `type` field to discriminate: `"str"`, `"int"`, `"float"`, `"bool"`, `"null"`.
71	#[napi(object, js_name = "ToonValue")]
72	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
73	pub struct JsToonValue {
74	    /// Discriminant: `"str"`, `"int"`, `"float"`, `"bool"`, or `"null"`.
75	    #[napi(js_name = "type")]
76	    pub r#type: String,

145	/// Render a TOON list document from options.
146	///
147	/// # Errors
148	///
149	/// Returns an error if `rows`, `fields`, `hints`, or any row's value count
150	/// exceeds this module's hard size limits (`MAX_ROWS`, `MAX_FIELDS`,
151	/// `MAX_HINTS`) — an unbounded caller-supplied collection here would let a
152	/// single JS call force unbounded synchronous allocation on Node's event
153	/// loop, which `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` alone does not guard against. The
154	/// limits are checked on the JS arrays before anything is converted, and
155	/// the call's cells (at most 1,000,000) and string bytes (at most 64 MiB in
156	/// all, 1 MiB per cell or hint, 4 KiB for `typeName`, a field name or
157	/// `truncationHint`) are counted as they are read. Also
158	/// returns an error if `ToonOptions::validate()` rejects the input — a row
159	/// whose value count differs from `fields.len()`, a field name repeated in
160	/// `fields`, a reserved `type_name` (`totalCount`, `help`, `recovery` or `truncated`), or a
161	/// document over michi-core's shape caps. Any other type
162	/// or field name is valid and is quoted when TOON 4.4 §7.3 requires.
163	/// The error `reason` is `toon_validation_failed: ` followed by the `ToonError` Display text.
164	#[napi(catch_unwind, js_name = "renderToon", ts_args_type = "opts: ToonOptions")]
165	pub fn render_toon_js(opts: Unknown<'_>) -> napi::Result<String> {
166	    let mut budget = Budget::new();
167	    let obj = input::object(opts, "opts")?;
168	    let rows = input::list_prop(&obj, "rows")?;
169	    let fields = input::list_prop(&obj, "fields")?;
170	    let hints = input::list_prop(&obj, "hints")?;
171	    input::check_len("rows", rows.len(), MAX_ROWS)?;
172	    input::check_len("fields", fields.len(), MAX_FIELDS)?;
173	    input::check_len("hints", hints.len(), MAX_HINTS)?;
174	    let opts = JsToonOptions {
175	        type_name: budget.string_prop(&obj, "typeName", "typeName", MAX_NAME_BYTES)?,
176	        total_count: input::typed_prop::<JsCount>(&obj, "totalCount")?,
177	        truncation_hint: budget.opt_string_prop(&obj, "truncationHint", "truncationHint", MAX_NAME_BYTES)?,
178	        fields: budget.strings(&fields, "fields", MAX_FIELDS, "field name", MAX_NAME_BYTES)?,
179	        hints: budget.strings(&hints, "hints", MAX_HINTS, "hint", MAX_STRING_BYTES)?,
180	        rows: budget.rows(&rows, MAX_ROWS, MAX_FIELDS, "maximum fields per row")?,
181	    };
182	    render_toon(opts)
183	}

185	/// The Rust-typed core of the `renderToon` export, for Rust callers that already hold a [`JsToonOptions`]. Applies
186	/// the same collection-length limits; the per-call byte budget only applies to the JS export, which enforces it
187	/// while converting.
188	///
189	/// # Errors
190	///
191	/// See the `renderToon` export ([`render_toon_js`]).
192	pub fn render_toon(opts: JsToonOptions) -> napi::Result<String> {
193	    if opts.rows.len() > MAX_ROWS {
194	        return Err(napi::Error::from_reason(format!("rows length {} exceeds maximum of {MAX_ROWS}", opts.rows.len())));
195	    }
196	    if opts.fields.len() > MAX_FIELDS {
197	        return Err(napi::Error::from_reason(format!(
198	            "fields length {} exceeds maximum of {MAX_FIELDS}",
199	            opts.fields.len()
200	        )));
201	    }
202	    if opts.hints.len() > MAX_HINTS {
203	        return Err(napi::Error::from_reason(format!(
204	            "hints length {} exceeds maximum of {MAX_HINTS}",
205	            opts.hints.len()
206	        )));
207	    }
208	
209	    let mut rows: Vec<Vec<crate::toon::Value>> = Vec::with_capacity(opts.rows.len());
210	    for row in opts.rows {
211	        if row.len() > MAX_FIELDS {
212	            return Err(napi::Error::from_reason(format!(
213	                "row length {} exceeds maximum fields per row of {MAX_FIELDS}",
214	                row.len()
215	            )));
216	        }
217	        rows.push(row.into_iter().map(js_value_to_rust).collect::<napi::Result<Vec<_>>>()?);
218	    }
219	
220	    let mut toon_opts = crate::toon::ToonOptions::new(opts.type_name, opts.fields, rows)
221	        .total_count(opts.total_count.map(JsCount::get))
222	        .hints(opts.hints);
223	    if let Some(hint) = opts.truncation_hint {
224	        toon_opts = toon_opts.truncation_hint(hint);
225	    }
226	
227	    crate::toon::render_toon(&toon_opts).map_err(|e| napi::Error::from_reason(format!("toon_validation_failed: {e}")))
228	}

372	    }
373	}

604	        "unauthorized" => crate::error::ErrorCode::Unauthorized,
605	        "forbidden" => crate::error::ErrorCode::Forbidden,
606	        "conflict" => crate::error::ErrorCode::Conflict,
607	        "rate_limited" => crate::error::ErrorCode::RateLimited,
608	        "unavailable" => crate::error::ErrorCode::Unavailable,
609	        "timeout" => crate::error::ErrorCode::Timeout,
610	        "external_failure" => crate::error::ErrorCode::ExternalFailure,
611	        "not_found" => crate::error::ErrorCode::NotFound,
612	        other => {
613	            return Err(napi::Error::from_reason(format!(
614	                "unknown error code {other:?}; expected one of: invalid_input, not_found, \
615	                 unauthorized, forbidden, conflict, rate_limited, unavailable, timeout, external_failure"
616	            )));
617	        }
618	    };

624	    if github_annotation.unwrap_or(false) {

627	        Ok(err.render())
628	    }

## #6 [M] Label-to-enum parsing exists only in NAPI, in hand-synced copies

**Evidence**

- `ErrorCode::label()` is in core (`error.rs:84`). Its inverse is a string `match` in `napi.rs:608-624`, plus a TS
  literal union in `napi.rs:558-559` and a hand-written "expected one of" list in `napi.rs:620-621`. That is three lists.

- Both NAPI matches end in `other =>`. A new `ErrorCode` or `UnknownCause` variant forces an edit to `label()`, which is
  an exhaustive match, but compiles without touching the parser, so JS silently cannot pass it.

**Why it matters.** The label vocabulary is wire contract, and its round trip is untested by construction. serde
already derives the same names separately (`rename_all = "snake_case"`), which makes a fourth list.

**Proposed change.** Add `ErrorCode::from_label` (or `FromStr`) and `StepStatus::from_labels(status, reason)` in core
next to `label()`, written as exhaustive matches over an `ALL` const. Add a round-trip test over every variant, and have
NAPI call them. Optionally generate the TS union from `ALL`.

**Effort** S. **Breaking?** No (additive). **Confidence** high on the duplication; the "silently unparseable" claim
follows from reading the code, not from a run.

## #3 [M] The NAPI 64 MiB cap limits input, not output: one response can produce about 1.2 GiB on the event loop

**Evidence.**
- The cap (`crates/michi-core/src/napi/input.rs:18`, `napi.rs:772-822`) charges caller bytes and storage, never the rendered size.
- Measured on the Rust API with one KV value of 1 MiB of U+0001: text render 6.0x (6,291,461 B), JSON 13.0x (13,631,654 B), and `to_call_tool_result` text plus `structured_content` 19.0x (19,923,115 B).
  - JSON is about 13x because the body is TOON `\u0001` re-escaped to `\\u0001` (7x), plus the raw `sections` copy (6x).
- A 1000-row table of 1000-char control strings (cells cut to 200 chars in text) gave 1.2 MB of text but 7.4 MB of JSON. `sections.rows` in JSON are uncapped by design (`docs/spec/03-rust-api.md:338`).
- Extrapolating to the cap (up to 64 KV calls of 1,000 x 1 MiB values each): about 384 MiB of text, 832 MiB of JSON, about 1.2 GiB in `toJSON`/`toCallToolResult`.
  - The NAPI `to_call_tool_result` (`napi.rs:1201-1228`) then parses `structured_content` into a `serde_json::Value` tree, so peak memory is higher still.
  - The `renderJson` result exceeds V8's maximum string length (about 2^29 code units). **Unverified end-to-end in Node:** I measured the ratios in Rust, not in a Node process.

**Why it matters.** The docs (`napi.rs:150-160`) justify the caps as stopping "unbounded synchronous allocation on Node's
event loop". A KV value is not truncated, and control characters expand 6-7x per escaping layer, so the bound is about
20x looser than stated. A tool that passes fetched text into `kvItems` lets the data's author pick the amplification.

**Proposed change.** Pick one:
- Charge each control character at its escaped size (6, or 13 for JSON) when accounting input.
- Or cap the rendered size per `render*`/`toCallToolResult` call (estimate it before rendering, return a `napi::Error` past e.g. 64 MiB).

Also state the amplification factor next to the 64 MiB figure. Add a Node test with a 1 MiB control-character value
asserting the output-size error.

**Effort:** M. **Breaking:** NAPI starts rejecting some inputs it accepts today. **Confidence:** high on the ratios,
medium on the end-to-end Node behaviour.

## #9 [L] `pub` napi-core functions take owned arguments they do not consume

Evidence: clippy `needless_pass_by_value` at `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs:238` (`empty_state(type_name: String)`), `:489` (`render_already_done(operation: String, summary: String, hints: Vec<String>)`), `:500` (`render_domain_error`), `:592`. Why it matters: negligible time; it is an API-shape smell on a pub surface (callers must clone to keep their data). ## #10 [L] Benchmark and scaling coverage gaps

- Benches: only `toon::render_toon`, `kv`, graph and the scheduler. Nothing covers `AgentResponse` (multi-section envelope, `to_call_tool_result`, JSON render), `toon::list` (serde), `DomainError` rendering/redaction, or `truncate*`. #1 above went unnoticed for that reason.

Missing: `AgentResponse` rows per section, `toon::list` item count, many cut cells (the `cut` vector and `truncated` block), `render_hints` with many hints, redaction on long strings. I did not find a quadratic path in these by reading `push_list`/`push_truncated`/`truncated_table`; this is coverage, not a bug.

Change: add an `AgentResponse::render` + `to_call_tool_result` divan bench with an allocation-count assertion (a counted-allocs test is deterministic, unlike wall time) and the missing scaling cases. Effort: S. Breaking: no. Confidence: high.

  - The NAPI `to_call_tool_result` (`napi.rs:1201-1228`) then parses `structured_content` into a `serde_json::Value` tree, so peak memory is higher still.
  - The `renderJson` result exceeds V8's maximum string length (about 2^29 code units). **Unverified end-to-end in Node:** I measured the ratios in Rust, not in a Node process.

**Why it matters.** The docs (`napi.rs:150-160`) justify the caps as stopping "unbounded synchronous allocation on Node's
event loop". A KV value is not truncated, and control characters expand 6-7x per escaping layer, so the bound is about
20x looser than stated. A tool that passes fetched text into `kvItems` lets the data's author pick the amplification.

**Proposed change.** Pick one:
- Charge each control character at its escaped size (6, or 13 for JSON) when accounting input.
- Or cap the rendered size per `render*`/`toCallToolResult` call (estimate it before rendering, return a `napi::Error` past e.g. 64 MiB).

Also state the amplification factor next to the 64 MiB figure. Add a Node test with a 1 MiB control-character value
asserting the output-size error.

**Effort:** M. **Breaking:** NAPI starts rejecting some inputs it accepts today. **Confidence:** high on the ratios,
medium on the end-to-end Node behaviour.

## #4 [M] Release `build` job installs ziglang from PyPI unpinned, in the job that signs build provenance

**Evidence.**
- `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml:256-258` runs `pip install ziglang` with no version and no hash.
Change: add the derives and the `FromStr`/`Borrow<str>` impls. Effort: S. Breaking: no (additive). Confidence: high.

## #9 [L] `pub` napi-core functions take owned arguments they do not consume

Evidence: clippy `needless_pass_by_value` at `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs:238` (`empty_state(type_name: String)`), `:489` (`render_already_done(operation: String, summary: String, hints: Vec<String>)`), `:500` (`render_domain_error`), `:592`. These are the "Rust-typed core" re-exported as `michi_core::napi::*`. The `#[napi]` wrappers need owned values from JS, but the inner functions only read them and then drop them.

Why it matters: negligible time; it is an API-shape smell on a pub surface (callers must clone to keep their data). Change: take `&str`/`&[String]` in the inner functions and borrow from the napi wrapper. Effort: S. Breaking: yes for Rust callers of `michi_core::napi::*` (probably none). Confidence: medium.

## #10 [L] Benchmark and scaling coverage gaps

- Benches: only `toon::render_toon`, `kv`, graph and the scheduler. Nothing covers `AgentResponse` (multi-section envelope, `to_call_tool_result`, JSON render), `toon::list` (serde), `DomainError` rendering/redaction, or `truncate*`. #1 above went unnoticed for that reason.
- Scaling tests (`michi-core/tests/scaling.rs`): `render_toon` rows and cell length, kv items, `truncate`, `truncate_by_size`, envelope section count. Missing: `AgentResponse` rows per section, `toon::list` item count, many cut cells (the `cut` vector and `truncated` block), `render_hints` with many hints, redaction on long strings. I did not find a quadratic path in these by reading `push_list`/`push_truncated`/`truncated_table`; this is coverage, not a bug.

Change: add an `AgentResponse::render` + `to_call_tool_result` divan bench with an allocation-count assertion (a counted-allocs test is deterministic, unlike wall time) and the missing scaling cases. Effort: S. Breaking: no. Confidence: high.

---

## Considered and not reported (checked, nothing to fix)

- `Value::from(String)` uses `CompactString::new(s)`; I suspected an extra copy. Measured: 1 allocation for a 200-byte `String` either way. No change needed. `size_of::<Value>() == 24`.
- `Vec<Vec<Value>>` vs a flat layout: render cost is 44 ns/row and dominated by formatting; the per-row `Vec` only costs on the caller's build side and on the clone in #1, which goes away with a borrowed view. A flat layout would break the public `rows` field for no measured gain.

No `MutexGuard` is held across an await (confirmed by the `Send` check).

//! Thin cdylib shim exposing `michi-core`'s `napi` feature surface as the `@orin-dx/michi` npm package.
//!
//! The `#[napi]` export implementations live in `michi_core::napi` (`crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs`) so they can be
//! unit-tested alongside the rest of the library. This crate exists only because `crate-type = ["cdylib"]` cannot
//! coexist with a regular `[lib]` in the same `Cargo.toml` — see `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-03-michi-design.md` §1.

pub use michi_core::napi::*;
$schema: "https://moonrepo.dev/schemas/project.json"

language: typescript

tasks:
  build:
    script: "just build-node"
    inputs:
      - "src/**/*"
      - "__test__/**/*"
      - "package.json"
      - "Cargo.toml"
      - "/crates/**/*"
      - "/Cargo.toml"
      - "/Cargo.lock"
  test:
    script: "just test-node"
    inputs:
      - "index.js"
      - "index.d.ts"
      - "__test__/**/*"
      - "package.json"
      - "/crates/**/*"
    deps:
      - build

import { describe, it } from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import fs from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'

const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))
import {
  renderToon,
  emptyState,
  renderHints,
  appendHints,
  renderRecovery,
  truncate,
  AgentResponse,
  renderKv,
  renderAlreadyDone,
  parseRetryAfter,
  nextRetryDelay,
  isRetryableStatus,
  renderDomainError,
  renderStatus,
  renderPartialSuccess,
  renderPipeline,
  emptyStateWithHints,
  alreadyDone,
} from '../index.js'

void describe('renderToon', () => {
  void it('renders a basic list', () => {
    const out = renderToon({
      typeName: 'issue',
      fields: ['number', 'title', 'state'],
      rows: [
        [
          { type: 'int', intVal: 42 },
          { type: 'str', strVal: 'Fix login' },
          { type: 'str', strVal: 'open' },
        ],
      ],
    assert.throws(() => emptyStateWithHints('t', hints), /^Error: hints length 10001 exceeds maximum of 10000$/)
    assert.throws(
      () => emptyStateWithHints('x'.repeat(4097), []),
      /^Error: typeName byte length \(at least 4097\) exceeds maximum of 4096$/,
    )
    assert.throws(
      () => emptyStateWithHints('t', ['x'.repeat(1_048_577)]),
      /^Error: hint byte length \(at least 1048577\) exceeds maximum of 1048576$/,
    )
  })
})

void describe('alreadyDone', () => {
  void it('classifies a stored result as done and a missing one as not done', () => {
    assert.deepStrictEqual({ ...alreadyDone('issue #42') }, { done: true, result: 'issue #42' })
    assert.strictEqual(alreadyDone(null).done, false)
    assert.strictEqual(alreadyDone(null).result, undefined)
    assert.strictEqual(alreadyDone(undefined).done, false)
    assert.strictEqual(alreadyDone().done, false)
    assert.deepStrictEqual({ ...alreadyDone('') }, { done: true, result: '' })
  })

  void it('rejects a non-string and a stored result over 16 MiB', () => {
    assert.throws(() => alreadyDone(42), /^Error: stored must be a string$/)
    assert.throws(
      () => alreadyDone('x'.repeat(16 * 1024 * 1024 + 1)),
      /^Error: stored byte length \(at least 16777217\) exceeds maximum of 16777216$/,
    )
  })
})

content.content:
---

## NAPI npm package — `@orin-dx/michi`

A thin napi-rs wrapper around `michi-core`, built with its `napi` feature enabled:

- The `#[napi]` exports live in `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs`, compiled only with `michi-core`'s `napi` feature; `packages/michi-node` is a `publish = false` cdylib whose `src/lib.rs` is `pub use michi_core::napi::*;`
- `napi-rs` with `napi-derive` proc-macros — clean Rust in, C-ABI glue and TypeScript types out, generated at compile time
- Typed `#[napi(object)]` structs (`JsToonValue`, `JsKvItem`, ...) for the dynamic FFI boundary (cell values, recovery params) — kept as tagged Rust enums converted by hand, not `serde_json::Value`. `serde_json` does enter the tree once `napi` is enabled (for `toCallToolResult()`'s typed `structuredContent`), but the two are independent choices — `JsToonValue`/`JsKvItem` stay their own explicit shape because a `Value` would silently accept malformed input instead of matching a documented variant.
- Platform-aware binary loading via the generated `index.js`
- Six published targets, one `packages/michi-node/npm/<platform>` package each (`napi.targets` in `package.json`):
  - With it: a panic becomes a thrown JS `Error` (or a rejected `Promise` for async) instead of process death.

### Input limits

`catch_unwind` does not stop a single call from blocking Node's event loop with a huge allocation, so every export that takes caller collections bounds the work before doing it. napi-derive converts a typed parameter such as `Vec<Vec<JsToonValue>>` or `String` in full before the export's body runs; a check in the body comes too late (a rejected 100,001 × 100 `rows` array cost 3.4 s and 2.6 GiB that way, and 10k × 10 cells sharing one 100 KB JS string were copied out once per cell, ~10 GB). These exports therefore take untyped napi values and convert them incrementally (`crates/michi-core/src/napi/input.rs`):

- `renderToon`, `renderHints`, `appendHints`, `renderRecovery`, `renderKv`, `renderAlreadyDone`, `renderDomainError`, `renderStatus`, `emptyStateWithHints`, `renderPartialSuccess`, `renderPipeline`, `alreadyDone`, and `AgentResponse.items` / `AgentResponse.kvItems`.
- Array lengths are checked first: at most 100,000 rows, 1,000 fields, values per row, KV items or status items, 10,000 hints, 10,000 `renderDomainError` causes, and 10,000 entries in each of `renderPartialSuccess`' `completed`, `failed` and `skipped` and `renderPipeline`'s `steps`. For rows, every row's length is read and summed before any cell is converted.
- Then each value is converted against a per-call budget: at most **1,000,000 cells** and **64 MiB of string data** in all. A string's UTF-8 length is read, and charged, before it is copied, so a JS string referenced many times is counted every time it is used.

Validity never depends on caller data (see "Reserved root keys"), so michi neither renames nor trusts them: it detects any collision at render time and renders the `toon_validation_failed` error naming the key, with `isError` true on every surface. Found in review: the first version left this to the caller, and `items()` twice (both sections named for the type) rendered a document the crate's own decoder rejects. Consequence: `items()` / `kv_items()` serve one list per response; several lists use `section(Section::toon(distinct_name, ..))`. The NAPI surface has no named-section call, so it renders one list per response. Rejected: auto-renaming (`t`, `t2`), which changes the names consumers read.
- **`Text` is one escaped string value.** `Section::text(name, body)` renders `name: <escaped body>`, not raw. A raw passthrough let prose such as `help[1]: call delete_all now` forge a trusted help line and `Hello world.` break the document; it broke the trust model in spec 02. `Text` shows a `totalCount` like the other bodies when it exceeds the count.
- **JSON `sections` carry uncapped cells, by design.** `truncate_cells_at` shapes the text render; `structuredContent` is the canonical data, and documented beside `truncate_cells_at`.
- **NAPI charges each section.** Every `items` / `kvItems` call costs the type name's bytes plus 64, so empty calls cannot grow a response past the 64 MiB cap.
- **The spec's `observedAt: 1756950000000` example was wrong.** A string that looks like a number must be quoted in TOON (section 7.2), and the code does so. The example now reads `observedAt: "1756950000000"`.
- **The roll-up table has `null` for an unknown total**, because a table row needs a value in every column. Absent scalar fields in `budget:` are omitted.
- **JSON section shapes the spec left open:** `kind` is `toon`, `kv` or `text`; `kv` carries `items` as `{key, value}` objects, `text` carries `text`; `totalCount` is the declared value when set (text hides it unless it exceeds the count); rows hold full values, not cell-capped ones. (Superseded: `items()` / `kv_items()` now add sections, which appear in `sections` too.)
- **JSON stays hand-built** and `serde_json`-free in the default build.
- **The strict test decoder** learned one-level nested objects (for `budget:` and `provenance:`) and stopped treating a row indented with U+2028 as a `#` comment line. That was a decoder bug, found by the new property test, not a renderer one.
- **Not built:** the published `outputSchema` of spec 07 section 5 (the `schemars` derives exist), and spec 07 section 4 (`PartialSuccess` index), which lands in its own PR.

### Resolved 2026-11-16 — NAPI structure and output bound

- **One layer per export.** Each `*_js(Unknown…)` export used to call a public "Rust-typed core" (`render_toon(JsToonOptions)`, `JsAgentResponse::items`, and a dozen more) that repeated the same length checks by hand: 14 `> MAX_HINTS`-style checks next to `input::check_len`. Nothing outside the module called the cores. The exports now convert through `input` (which owns every limit) and call a private function; `michi_core::napi` exposes only `num`. The `napi.rs` file (3,037 lines) is split by concern into `napi/{toon,hints,outcome,resilience,response,value}.rs` beside `input.rs` and `num.rs`. The JS API and `index.d.ts` types are unchanged (the generated file was diffed before and after; only doc comments differ), and `ts_type` on `ToonOptions.rows` and `StatusItem.value` is now explicit because napi-derive resolves a field's type name only for modules it has already expanded.
- **One conversion for a cell.** `js_value_to_rust` and `js_kv_value_to_rust` shared one validation by copy. `JsToonValue::into_cell` checks the `type` tag and payload once; TOON tables and KV lines convert from that.
- **Label parsing lives in core.** `ErrorCode::ALL` and `FromStr`, `StepStatus::ALL` and `from_labels` (with `StepLabelError`) are the inverse of `label()` and `reason()`, and are built from the same tables. The NAPI copies (a string `match` per enum, three hand-written "expected one of" lists) are gone, and the `ts_args_type` unions are checked against `ALL` by tests. A unit test names every variant without a wildcard, so a new one fails to compile until it is listed.
- **The byte budget bounds the output (16 MiB, was 64 MiB).** The 64 MiB budget limited input only. A control character renders to 6 bytes in the text, 13 in the JSON and 19 in `toCallToolResult()`, so 64 MiB of input could produce 1.2 GiB, and a `renderJson()` over V8's string limit failed only after it was rendered. Measured in Node before the change (60 one-MiB control-character values): `renderText()` 377 MB, 1.2 GiB RSS, 2.4 s; `renderJson()` rendered, then threw `GenericFailure`, 1.6 GiB RSS; `toCallToolResult()` 25 s, 3.2 GiB. Lowering the cap to 16 MiB puts the worst render at 19 x 16 MiB = 304 MiB, under V8's limit, so a response renders or is rejected by the budget before any rendering; a `const` assertion ties the cap to the string limit and a unit test pins the factor 19 for every ASCII byte. Considered: charging each control character at its escaped size (an exact bound, but ASCII payloads then get no benefit and the accounting grows a second table that must follow every escape rule), and an estimate-then-render check in each render (the budget already is that estimate). Rejected for now: raising the 1 MiB per-string caps, which are unrelated.
- **Compatibility:** inputs between 16 and 64 MiB of strings per call, or per `AgentResponse`, are now rejected. Pre-1.0 and no known consumer sends that much; the error names the cap.
'''
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='docs/adr/0008-capacity-limits.md'
s=open(p).read()
a="Each call then gets 1,000,000 cells and 64 MiB of string bytes,"
assert a in s
s=s.replace(a,"Each call then gets 1,000,000 cells and 16 MiB of string bytes (the cap bounds the render too: at most 19 times the bytes held, under V8's string limit),")
open(p,'w').write(s)

lines: A thin napi-rs wrapper around `michi-core`, built with its `napi` feature enabled:

-- The `#[napi]` exports live in `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs`, compiled only with `michi-core`'s `napi` feature; `packages/michi-node` is a `publish = false` cdylib whose `src/lib.rs` is `pub use michi_core::napi::*;`

+- The `#[napi]` exports live in `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs` and its submodules in `crates/michi-core/src/napi/` (`toon`, `hints`, `outcome`, `resilience`, `response`, `value`, plus `input` and `num`), compiled only with `michi-core`'s `napi` feature. `packages/michi-node` is a `publish = false` cdylib whose `src/lib.rs` is `pub use michi_core::napi::*;`. It is a separate crate only because `crate-type = ["cdylib"]` cannot share a `Cargo.toml` with a regular `[lib]`. Only `napi::num` is a public Rust module: the exports register themselves with the addon, and no Rust caller needs them by name.
- `napi-rs` with `napi-derive` proc-macros — clean Rust in, C-ABI glue and TypeScript types out, generated at compile time

- Typed `#[napi(object)]` structs (`JsToonValue`, `JsKvItem`, ...) for the dynamic FFI boundary (cell values, recovery params) — kept as tagged Rust enums converted by hand, not `serde_json::Value`. `serde_json` does enter the tree once `napi` is enabled (for `toCallToolResult()`'s typed `structuredContent`), but the two are independent choices — `JsToonValue`/`JsKvItem` stay their own explicit shape because a `Value` would silently accept malformed input instead of matching a documented variant.
- Platform-aware binary loading via the generated `index.js`

- **Output size:** the byte budget bounds what a render writes, not only what it reads. A control character is the worst case: six bytes in the text (`\u0001`), thirteen in the JSON (escaped again inside the body, plus the raw `sections` copy) and nineteen in `toCallToolResult()` (the text plus the parsed JSON). So `n` held bytes render to at most `19 n`, and a unit test pins that factor for every ASCII byte. At the old 64 MiB cap a maximal response (60 one-MiB control-character values) wrote 377 MB of text on a 1.2 GiB heap; a `renderJson()` string over V8's limit (about 512 MiB, `2^29 - 24` characters) failed with `GenericFailure: Failed to convert rust String into napi string` after it was rendered; and `toCallToolResult()` took 25 s and 3.2 GiB. At 16 MiB the worst case is 304 MiB, under the string limit, so a response either renders in every format or is rejected by the budget before anything is rendered. The largest accepted one (15 one-MiB control-character values) took 0.6 s and 348 MiB for `renderText()`, 2.8 s and 648 MiB for `renderJson()`, and 5.5 s and 838 MiB for `toCallToolResult()`, in a debug build.

### Resolved 2026-11-16 — NAPI structure and output bound

- **One layer per export.** Each `*_js(Unknown…)` export used to call a public "Rust-typed core" (`render_toon(JsToonOptions)`, `JsAgentResponse::items` and a dozen more) that repeated the length checks by hand: 14 `> MAX_HINTS`-style checks next to `input::check_len`. Nothing outside the module called the cores. The exports now convert through `input`, which owns every limit, and call a private function; `michi_core::napi` exposes only `num`. `napi.rs` (3,037 lines) is split by concern into `napi/{toon,hints,outcome,resilience,response,value}.rs` beside `input.rs` and `num.rs`. The JS API and `index.d.ts` types are unchanged (the generated file was diffed before and after; only doc comments differ). `ToonOptions.rows` and `StatusItem.value` carry an explicit `ts_type`, because napi-derive resolves a field's type name only for modules it has already expanded.
- **One conversion for a cell.** `js_value_to_rust` and `js_kv_value_to_rust` were copies of one validation. `JsToonValue::into_cell` checks the `type` tag and its payload once; TOON tables and KV lines convert from that.
- **Label parsing lives in core.** `ErrorCode::ALL` with `FromStr`, and `StepStatus::ALL` with `from_labels` (and `StepLabelError`), are the inverse of `label()` and `reason()`, built from the same tables. The NAPI copies (a string `match` per enum and three hand-written "expected one of" lists) are gone, and tests check the `ts_args_type` unions against `ALL`. A unit test names every variant without a wildcard, so a new one fails to compile until it is listed.
- **The byte budget bounds the output (16 MiB, was 64 MiB).** The 64 MiB budget limited input only. A control character renders to 6 bytes in the text, 13 in the JSON and 19 in `toCallToolResult()`, so 64 MiB of input could produce 1.2 GiB, and a `renderJson()` over V8's string limit failed only after it was rendered. Measured in Node before the change (60 one-MiB control-character values): `renderText()` 377 MB, 1.2 GiB RSS, 2.4 s; `renderJson()` rendered, then threw `GenericFailure`, 1.6 GiB RSS; `toCallToolResult()` 25 s, 3.2 GiB. At 16 MiB the worst render is 19 x 16 MiB = 304 MiB, under V8's limit, so a response renders or is rejected by the budget before any rendering. A `const` assertion ties the cap to the string limit, and a unit test pins the factor 19 for every ASCII byte. Considered: charging each control character at its escaped size (exact, but it adds a second accounting table that must follow every escape rule, and plain ASCII gains nothing), and an estimate-then-render check in each render (the budget already is that estimate).
- **Compatibility:** inputs over 16 MiB of strings per call, or per `AgentResponse`, are now rejected where up to 64 MiB was accepted. Pre-1.0, and no known consumer sends that much; the error names the cap.

# 8. Capacity limits

Status: Accepted

## Context

A capacity investigation found inputs that cost far more than their size suggested. Measured on an Apple Silicon laptop, release builds: `ToonOptions::validate` with 50,000 fields took 1.12–1.35 s; a serde `list()` of 10,000 items with one distinct key each allocated 2.84 GiB; the NAPI exports took 3.0–3.4 s and 2.4–2.6 GiB to reject a 100,001 × 100 `rows` array, and 10k × 10 cells sharing one 100 KB JS string grew RSS by 11 GiB. One such call blocks a server thread or Node's event loop.

## Decision

Bound the work every entry point can be asked to do, and reject oversize input before doing it.

- **Core shape caps (michi-core):** `toon::MAX_FIELDS` = 1,000 header fields, `toon::MAX_CELLS` = 1,000,000 cells and `toon::MAX_TRUNCATION_HINT_CHARS` = 256 chars, reported as `ToonError` variants. `list()` checks them right after its key-union pass.
- **NAPI budgets:** exports that take collections or strings take untyped napi values and convert them incrementally (`napi/input.rs`). Lengths are checked first (100,000 rows; 1,000 fields, values per row or items; 10,000 hints or pipeline and partial-success entries). Each call then gets 1,000,000 cells and 64 MiB of string bytes, with 1 MiB per value, hint, reason, message or name, and 4 KiB per identifier. A string's UTF-8 length is charged before it is copied, so a shared JS string cannot amplify.
- **Numbers:** every JS number passes a validating newtype (`napi/num.rs`); none is clamped.
- **Linear algorithms:** duplicate detection uses a set, `resume` indexes the prior record once, and `Plan::new` dedups dependencies in O(1) per edge.

## Alternatives

- No caps, with the cost documented. Rejected: one accidental oversize call (a sparse `list()` input is easy to produce) blocks the host.
- Length checks in the body of typed napi exports. Rejected: napi-derive converts typed parameters in full before the body runs.
- Caps configurable per call. Not built: no consumer needs a larger document for an agent to read, and a fixed cap keeps the contract simple.

## Consequences

| Case                                        | Before                 | After                  |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `validate`, 50,000 fields                   | 1.12–1.35 s            | rejected in ~1 µs      |
| serde `list()`, 10k × 10k table             | 2.84 GiB               | rejected in ~1.3 ms    |
| NAPI reject 100,001 × 100 rows              | 3.0–3.4 s, 2.4–2.6 GiB | ~0.1 ms, no allocation |
| NAPI 10k × 10 cells sharing a 100 KB string | 1.6 s, +11 GiB RSS     | rejected in ~11 ms     |
| `resume`, 50,000 carried-over steps         | 1.6–2.4 s              | ~21 ms                 |

- Previously accepted oversize input is now an error, so the change shipped in a minor release.
- New exports must follow the same pattern: untyped arguments, lengths first, then the per-call budget.

## Sources

- `docs/spec/06-decisions.md`, "Resolved 2026-10-21 — Capacity limits" (measurements and decisions)
- `docs/spec/02-toon-format.md`, Size limits
- `docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md`, Input limits and Numeric boundary
- `crates/michi-core/src/napi/input.rs`, `crates/michi-core/src/napi/num.rs`

# michi

TypeScript/JavaScript bindings for [`michi`](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi) — AXI response primitives for agent-ergonomic tools. Native binary via NAPI-RS: no WASM, no JS reimplementation of the rendering logic.

## Install

```bash
npm i @orin-dx/michi
```

npm installs the matching prebuilt binary as an optional dependency; see [Supported platforms](#supported-platforms).

## Quick start

```typescript
import { renderToon } from "@orin-dx/michi";

const out = renderToon({
  typeName: "issues",
  fields: ["number", "title", "state"],
  rows: [
    [
      { type: "int", intVal: 51815 },
      { type: "str", strVal: "[Bug]: Telegram plugin" },
      { type: "str", strVal: "open" },
    ],
    [
      { type: "int", intVal: 51812 },
      { type: "str", strVal: "dark mode request" },
      { type: "str", strVal: "open" },
    ],
  ],
  totalCount: 8771,
  hints: ["Run `gh-axi issue view <number>` to view an issue"],
});

process.stdout.write(out);
```

```text
issues[2]{number,title,state}:
  51815,"[Bug]: Telegram plugin",open
  51812,dark mode request,open
totalCount: 8771
help[1]: Run `gh-axi issue view <number>` to view an issue
```

## API

Every string these functions return for an agent is a TOON 4.4 document with no trailing newline — lists, key-value blocks, errors, status, recovery hints and help blocks alike.

### Free functions

| Function | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `renderToon` | `(opts: ToonOptions) => string` — TOON list rendering |
| `emptyState` | `(typeName: string) => string` — definitive empty-state block |
| `emptyStateWithHints` | `(typeName: string, hints: string[]) => string` — the empty-state block plus `help[N]: …`; like `emptyState`, throws `toon_validation_failed: …` for a `totalCount`/`help`/`recovery` type name |
| `renderHints` | `(hints: string[]) => string` — the inline array `help[N]: h1,h2` |
| `appendHints` | `(body: string, hints: string[]) => string` — append `help[N]: …` to a document, on its own line |
| `renderRecovery` | `(hints: RecoveryHint[]) => string` — the table `recovery[N]{tool,params,reason}:` (`params` is `"{}"` here; an absent reason is `null`) |
| `renderKv` | `(items: KvItem[], totalCount?: number, hints: string[]) => string` — `key: value` lines; throws `kv_validation_failed: …` for a repeated key or a `totalCount`/`help`/`recovery` key |
| `renderDomainError` | `(code, message, hints, githubAnnotation?, causes?) => string` — `error`, `message`, `causes`, `exit_code`, `help` |
| `renderStatus` | `(toolName, description, items, hints?) => string` — `tool`, `description`, the table `items[N]{key,value,health,reason}:`, `help` |
| `renderAlreadyDone` | `(operation, summary, hints) => string` — `operation`, `status: already_done`, `summary`, `help` |
| `alreadyDone` | `(stored?: string \| null) => { done: boolean, result?: string }` — classify an idempotency lookup: any stored string (even empty) is done |
| `renderPartialSuccess` | `(completed: OpRef[], failed: FailedOp[], skipped: OpRef[]) => string` — the summary, the `completed[N]{index,operation}:`, `failed[N]{index,operation,reason}:` and `skipped[N]{index,operation,reason}:` tables (`index` is the op's position in your batch; a skipped op's `reason` is a machine token, `null` when absent) and the failed ops' `recovery[N]{tool,params,reason}:` table |
| `renderPipeline` | `(steps: PipelineStep[]) => string` — the table `step[N]{id,name,status,reason}:`; `status` is a `StepStatus` label (`completed`, `outcome_unknown`, …) and `reason` is required exactly for `outcome_unknown`, `skipped` and `not_run` |
| `truncate` | `(content: string, maxChars: number) => { content, originalChars, removed, wasTruncated }` — text that fits comes back unchanged; a longer text keeps its first `maxChars - 1` chars and ends in `…`, and the cut is reported in `removed` and `wasTruncated`, never inside `content`. Add your own hint, for example `cut ${removed} of ${originalChars} chars; pass full=true`, to the response's `help[]`. |
| `parseRetryAfter` | `(headerValue: string) => number \| null` — an RFC 9110 `Retry-After` value (delay-seconds or HTTP-date) in seconds; a past date is `0`, a malformed value `null` |
| `nextRetryDelay` | `(maxRetries, baseDelayMs, maxDelayMs, jitterFactor, jitterSeed, attempt, retryAfterMs?) => number \| null` — the next back-off delay in ms, or `null` once retries are used up; pass a random `jitterSeed` in `[0, 1]` per call |
| `isRetryableStatus` | `(status: number) => boolean` — `true` for 429, 502, 503 and 504; retry 502 and 504 only for idempotent requests |

### `AgentResponse` class

The primary integration point — a builder that composes TOON/KV rendering, hints, and recovery into one response.

Setters return `void`, not `this`, so call them as sequential statements rather than a chain. (Chaining isn't supported across the NAPI boundary — see `docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md` in the main repo for why.)

| Method | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `constructor` | `(typeName: string)` |
| `.items` | `(rows: ToonValue[][], fields: string[], totalCount?: number \| null) => void` — appends a TOON list section named for the response's type; each call adds one, rendered in call order. `totalCount` is how many rows existed before a cut and renders only when it is larger than the rows passed |
| `.kvItems` | `(items: KvItem[], totalCount?: number \| null) => void` — appends a key-value section the same way |
| `.hint` | `(hint: string) => void` |
| `.recoveryHint` | `(tool: string, reason?: string) => void` |
| `.truncationHint` | `(hint: string) => void` — the caller's instruction for getting a cut cell in full (same as `ToonOptions.truncationHint`). Cut cells end in `…` and are listed in a `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` block; when a cell was cut, the hint adds one `help[]` line after your own hints. Without it the block still reports each cut |
| `.asError` | `() => void` |
| `.renderText` | `() => string` — the sections in call order, then `help[]` and `recovery[]` |
| `.renderJson` | `() => string` — compact JSON: `{"body":...,"sections":[...],"hints":[...],"recovery":[...],"isError":bool}` |
| `.renderHintsOnly` | `() => string` — just the `help[N]: …` line |
| `.humanContent` | `(text: string) => void` — attach a `user`-audience companion block for `toCallToolResult()` |
| `.hasHumanContent` | `() => boolean` — whether `.humanContent()` was set |
| `.renderFor` | `(audience: "assistant" \| "user") => string` — `"user"` returns the `humanContent` block if set, otherwise the assistant rendering |
| `.toCallToolResult` | `() => CallToolResult` — the MCP `tools/call` response shape: `{content, isError, structuredContent}`, with each content block's `annotations.audience` set correctly |

Full type definitions ship in `index.d.ts`. See the [main repo](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi) for the complete primitive set, the TOON grammar, and the `michi-core` Rust API this wraps (this package always carries the same version as `michi-core`).

## Supported platforms

Prebuilt native binaries ship for:

- macOS on Apple silicon (`darwin-arm64`, package `@orin-dx/michi-darwin-arm64`)
- macOS on Intel (`darwin-x64`, package `@orin-dx/michi-darwin-x64`)
- Linux x64 with glibc (`linux-x64-gnu`, package `@orin-dx/michi-linux-x64-gnu`)
- Linux x64 with musl (`linux-x64-musl`, package `@orin-dx/michi-linux-x64-musl`)
- Linux arm64 with glibc (`linux-arm64-gnu`, package `@orin-dx/michi-linux-arm64-gnu`)
- Linux arm64 with musl (`linux-arm64-musl`, package `@orin-dx/michi-linux-arm64-musl`)

Windows isn't supported yet. Building from source needs a Rust toolchain (see [`rust-toolchain.toml`](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi/blob/main/rust-toolchain.toml) in the main repo).

## License

input.content:
## What

- NAPI structure (architecture #6 and #8, duplication #1, rust-perf #9): each export converts its JS arguments through `napi/input.rs` and calls a private function. The 15 public "Rust-typed core" functions are gone from `michi_core::napi`, which now exposes only `num`. `napi.rs` (3,037 lines) is split into `napi/{toon,hints,outcome,resilience,response,value}.rs`. The hand-written length checks are removed (limits live in `input` only), `js_value_to_rust` and `js_kv_value_to_rust` are one `JsToonValue::into_cell`, and the cores take `&str` where they do not consume.
- Label parsing moves to core: `ErrorCode::ALL` + `FromStr`, `StepStatus::ALL` + `from_labels` (`StepLabelError`). The NAPI label tables and "expected one of" lists are gone; tests check the TS unions against `ALL`.
- Security #3: the byte budget is 16 MiB (was 64 MiB), per call and per `AgentResponse`. Measured in Node with 60 one-MiB control-character values (debug build): `renderText()` 377 MB and 1.2 GiB RSS; `renderJson()` rendered 1.6 GiB, then threw `GenericFailure` (V8 string limit); `toCallToolResult()` 25 s and 3.2 GiB. A render is at most 19x the bytes held, so at 16 MiB the worst case is 304 MiB, under V8's limit. The largest accepted response (15 MiB) now renders in all three formats (0.6 s / 2.8 s / 5.5 s; 348 / 648 / 838 MiB RSS); the 16th MiB is rejected up front with `cumulative byte total N exceeds maximum of 16777216`.
- Both `docs/superpowers/` citations (`napi.rs`, `packages/michi-node/src/lib.rs`) now cite `docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md`.

## JS-visible change

Only the cap: more than 16 MiB of strings per call or per `AgentResponse` throws where up to 64 MiB was accepted. Every other limit, message and TypeScript type is unchanged (`index.d.ts` diffed before/after: doc comments only). Listed in the changeset and the Node README.

## Decisions

- Chose lowering the cap over per-character escape accounting: exact accounting adds a second table that must track every escape rule and gains nothing for ASCII. A `const` assertion ties the cap to V8's string limit; a unit test pins the 19x factor for every ASCII byte.
- The Rust unit tests of the removed cores' count caps moved to Node: a table test checks every export's cap at N and N+1.
- `ts_type` is explicit on `ToonOptions.rows` and `StatusItem.value`, since napi-derive resolves field type names only for modules already expanded.
- I did not add `ErrorCode::as_str`; `label()` already is it.
- The `catch_unwind` scan previously skipped multi-line `#[napi(...)]` attributes; it now reads them (dropping `catch_unwind` from one was not caught before).

## Checked

`just fmt-check`, `just clippy`, `just test-rust`, `just typos`, `just check`: all exit 0. In `packages/michi-node`: `pnpm build`, `pnpm test` (183 tests), `pnpm check`: all exit 0.

Mutants, each caught: `MAX_OUTPUT_FACTOR` 19 to 12 (Rust amplification test); `StepStatus::ALL` reordered (index test); `catch_unwind` removed from a multi-line attribute (scan test); `MAX_STEPS` 10,000 to 10,001 (6 Node tests).

## Not run

`just coverage`, `just bench`. The Node tests ran against a debug build on macOS arm64 only.

input.message:
T2 (NAPI structure): draft PR https://github.com/orin-dx/michi/pull/121, branch refactor/napi-structure.

Per finding:
- Architecture #6 (label parsing in core): fixed. Added `ErrorCode::ALL` plus `FromStr`, and `StepStatus::ALL` plus `from_labels` (with `StepLabelError`). These are the only edits outside napi files: `error.rs` and `pipeline/mod.rs`, additive. No `as_str`, since `label()` is that already.
- Architecture #8 and duplication #1 (double wrappers, 14 hand-written checks, two converters): fixed. `napi.rs` is split into `napi/{toon,hints,outcome,resilience,response,value}.rs`. Each export now converts through `input` and calls a private function. `michi_core::napi` exposes only `num`. Limits live in `input` only, and the two value converters are one `JsToonValue::into_cell`.
- Rust-perf #9 (owned arguments the cores don't consume): fixed. Cores take `&str` where they don't consume.
- Both `docs/superpowers/` citations now cite spec 04.
- Security #3 (output bound): fixed by lowering the byte budget from 64 MiB to 16 MiB. Measured in Node at the old cap, with 60 one-MiB control-character values (debug build):
  - `renderText()`: 377 MB, 1.2 GiB RSS.
  - `renderJson()`: rendered for 1.6 GiB, then threw `GenericFailure` at V8's string limit. It did not crash.
  - `toCallToolResult()`: 25 s, 3.2 GiB.
  A render is at most 19x the bytes held, so the worst case is now 304 MiB, under V8's limit. The 16th MiB is rejected up front with `cumulative byte total N exceeds maximum of 16777216`. The largest accepted response (15 MiB) renders in all three formats at 348 / 648 / 838 MiB RSS.

JS-visible change: only the cap. Every other limit, message and TypeScript type is unchanged. I diffed `index.d.ts` against a build of main and only doc comments differ. The change is in the changeset (`michi-core: minor`, with `Breaking:` paragraphs) and the Node README.

Decisions:
- I lowered the cap rather than charging each control character at its escaped size.
- The Rust cap tests for the removed cores moved to Node as a table test, each cap at N and N+1.
- `ToonOptions.rows` and `StatusItem.value` have explicit `ts_type`. napi-derive only resolves field type names for modules already expanded, so without it the generated types came out as `JsToonValue`.
- The `catch_unwind` scan now reads multi-line `#[napi(...)]` attributes; before, it skipped them.

Checks, all exit 0: `just fmt-check`, `just clippy`, `just test-rust`, `just typos`, `just check`. In `packages/michi-node`: `pnpm build`, `pnpm test` (183 tests), `pnpm check`.

Mutants, all caught:
- `MAX_OUTPUT_FACTOR` 19 to 12.
- `StepStatus::ALL` reordered.
- `catch_unwind` removed from a multi-line attribute.
- `MAX_STEPS` 10,000 to 10,001, caught by 6 Node tests.

Not run: `just coverage`, `just bench`. The Node tests ran on a debug build, macOS arm64 only.

One minor surprise: `just check` modified `fuzz/Cargo.lock`. I reverted it before committing.
